title: Langevin dynamics towards Generalized Gibbs Ensembles
authors: Rafael González-Albaladejo, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, Gustavo S. Lozano, Daniel A. Stariolo
abstract: In recent years, statistical physics tools have been used to study the dynamics of macroscopic quantum and classical integrable models. These studies have shown that, in the thermodynamic limit, long term time-averages of local observables equal statistical averages calculated with a Generalized Gibbs Ensemble (GGE). In the latter, the weight in phase space involves all constants of motion multiplied by Lagrange multipliers which are fixed by their initial values. We argue that the GGE can be interpreted as a proper Boltzmann measure of a different (non-standard) mechanical model. This measure can therefore be sampled with stochastic methods implemented, for example, as a Langevin process. We tailor the deterministic force in the Langevin equations so that at long times the stochastic trajectories sample the desired measure. We use the integrable Neumann Model -- the model of a classical particle constrained to move on a sphere under anisotropic harmonic potentials -- as a benchmark. We test the method in a setup where the Lagrange multipliers are fixed by the GGE governing the asymptotic dynamics of the isolated Neumann model following a quench. This problem has different phases depending on the initial conditions and quench protocol and, in all cases, with the stochastic evolution of an adequately tuned Langevin process we reproduce the asymptotic values of relevant observables.
summary: This paper introduces the use of Langevin dynamics as a powerful stochastic tool to sample the Generalized Gibbs Ensemble (GGE) measure for integrable systems. By tailoring the deterministic force, the authors show that the long-time evolution of the system samples the GGE, which is rigorously tested and confirmed using the Neumann Model. This provides a robust method for calculating non-equilibrium steady states in complex physical models.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop and apply a stochastic method to efficiently sample the Generalized Gibbs Ensemble (GGE) measure for integrable quantum and classical systems.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate that a carefully tuned Langevin process can reproduce the asymptotic statistical averages predicted by the GGE for the Neumann Model following a quench.
method: The core method involves deriving the deterministic force for a Langevin process such that the long-time stochastic trajectories sample the desired GGE measure, which is shown to be equivalent to a standard Gibbs-Boltzmann measure for a modified Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The study uses the classical Neumann Model (a particle on a sphere with anisotropic potentials) as a benchmark, extending the analysis to the Generalized Neumann Model (GNM) which incorporates multiple conserved quantities (constants of motion).
key_observables: Asymptotic values of local observables, $\langle p^2(\lambda) angle$, and $\langle x^2(\lambda) angle$.

main_assumptions: The assumption that the GGE can be interpreted as a standard Boltzmann measure for a non-standard Hamiltonian, and that the Langevin process converges to this measure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate mode-resolved results for Langevin dynamics on the Neumann Model under different conditions relating the Lagrange multipliers ($ ar{\gamma}_\mu$ vs $ ar{\gamma}_N$), showing distinct dynamic regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the GGE framework for integrable systems, interpreting it as a standard Gibbs measure, developing the Langevin sampling technique, and finally applying this method to the Neumann Model, including detailed mathematical derivations for the Lagrange multipliers.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, computationally accessible stochastic tool (Langevin dynamics) to calculate equilibrium properties (GGE) in complex, non-equilibrium systems, which is highly relevant for understanding relaxation dynamics in many-body quantum systems.
